claim: Osteoblast-associated proteins (RUNX2, OSX, OCN, and COL1A1) are significantly enriched in proline compared to all proteins.
source: Using a bioinformatic approach, we discovered that osteoblast differentiation is associated with increased demand for the amino acid proline. When compared to other differentiated cells, osteoblast-associated proteins, including RUNX2, OSX, OCN, and COL1A1, are significantly enriched in proline.
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis presented in the manuscript, including data shown in Figure 1 and Tables 1-2.

claim: SLC38A2 acts cell-autonomously to provide proline to facilitate the efficient synthesis of proline-rich osteoblast proteins.
source: Using a genetic and metabolomic approach, we demonstrate that the neutral amino acid transporter SLC38A2 acts cell-autonomously to provide proline to facilitate the efficient synthesis of proline-rich osteoblast proteins.
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic ablation experiments and metabolomic analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Genetic ablation of SLC38A2 in osteoblasts limits both osteoblast differentiation and bone formation in mice.
source: Genetic ablation of SLC38A2 in osteoblasts limits both osteoblast differentiation and bone formation in mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo experiments using Slc38a2 knockout mice shown in Figure 5.

claim: Proline is primarily incorporated into nascent protein with little metabolism observed.
source: Mechanistically, proline is primarily incorporated into nascent protein with little metabolism observed.
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Osteoblast-associated proteins have a higher proline composition (7.1%) when compared to the average of all proteins (6.1%).
source: Osteoblast-associated proteins (GO:0001649) were found to have a higher proline composition when compared to the average of all proteins (7.1% vs. 6.1% proline for osteoblasts vs. all proteins) (Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis of protein amino acid composition presented in Table 2.

claim: Many classical osteoblast proteins (e.g., RUNX2, OSX, and COL1A1) were above the 90th percentile for proline composition.
source: In fact, many classical osteoblast proteins (e.g., RUNX2, OSX, and COL1A1) were above the 90th percentile for proline composition and 43.5% of all osteoblast proteins were above the 75th percentile for proline composition.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of proline composition in osteoblast proteins.

claim: 43.5% of all osteoblast proteins were above the 75th percentile for proline composition.
source: In fact, many classical osteoblast proteins (e.g., RUNX2, OSX, and COL1A1) were above the 90th percentile for proline composition and 43.5% of all osteoblast proteins were above the 75th percentile for proline composition.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of proline composition in osteoblast proteins.

claim: No other amino acids were similarly enriched in osteoblast-associated proteins compared to proline.
source: No other amino acids were similarly enriched in osteoblast-associated proteins (Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative analysis of amino acid composition shown in Table 2.

claim: Osteoblast-associated proteins were enriched for proline when compared to proteins associated with other cell types, including osteoclasts, cardiomyocytes, muscle cells, hematopoietic stem cells, endothelial cells, epithelial cells, or neurons.
source: Moreover, osteoblast-associated proteins were enriched for proline when compared to proteins associated with other cell types, including osteoclasts (GO:0030855), cardiomyocytes (GO:0001649), muscle cells (GO:0055007), hematopoietic stem cells (GO:0042692), endothelial cells (GO:0030182), epithelial cells (GO:0055007), or neurons (GO:0030182) (Figure 1B, Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 1B and Table 2.

claim: Alanine and cysteine enrichment was comparable amongst different cell types.
source: In contrast, alanine and cysteine enrichment was comparable amongst the different cell types (Figure 1B, Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 1B and Table 2.

claim: Proline was enriched in proteins encoded by genes induced during osteoblast differentiation compared to all genes or genes that were suppressed.
source: Consistent with our previous analysis, proline was enriched in proteins encoded by the induced genes compared to either all genes or genes that were suppressed in differentiated calvarial osteoblasts (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis and proline composition calculations shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Proline demand is predicted to rise during osteoblast differentiation.
source: Moreover, comparing the basal and differentiation-associated transcriptional changes with proline composition indicates that proline demand is predicted to rise, whereas the demand for alanine and cysteine is predicted to decline during osteoblast differentiation (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on computational predictions from transcriptomic data and amino acid composition analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The demand for alanine and cysteine is predicted to decline during osteoblast differentiation.
source: Moreover, comparing the basal and differentiation-associated transcriptional changes with proline composition indicates that proline demand is predicted to rise, whereas the demand for alanine and cysteine is predicted to decline during osteoblast differentiation (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on computational predictions from transcriptomic data and amino acid composition analysis.

claim: 10.5% of intracellular proline is synthesized from either glutamine (9.9%) or glucose (0.6%) in 24 hr in naïve calvarial cells.
source: 10.5% of intracellular proline is synthesized from either glutamine (9.9%) or glucose (0.6%) in 24 hr (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by stable isotope tracing experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 37.8% of the proline pool is labeled from 13CU-proline after 24 hr in naïve calvarial cells.
source: By comparison, 37.8% of the proline pool is labeled from 13CU-proline after 24 hr, and this increased to 66.6% after 72 hr (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 66.6% of the proline pool is labeled from 13CU-proline after 72 hr in naïve calvarial cells.
source: By comparison, 37.8% of the proline pool is labeled from 13CU-proline after 24 hr, and this increased to 66.6% after 72 hr (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The slow labeling of proline compared to intracellular glutamine suggests that in naïve calvarial cells proline uptake is slow and the intracellular proline pool is relatively stable with little turnover.
source: The slow labeling of proline when compared to intracellular glutamine that reached saturation within hours suggests that in naïve calvarial cells proline uptake is slow and the intracellular proline pool is relatively stable with little turnover.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from isotope labeling kinetics data.

claim: Proline uptake was slow compared to glutamine uptake in naïve cells.
source: Consistent with the labeling data, proline uptake was slow compared to glutamine uptake in naïve cells (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by radiolabeled amino acid uptake assays shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: During differentiation, the rate of proline uptake increased significantly and to a greater extent than glutamine in both primary bone marrow stromal cell and calvarial cultures.
source: During differentiation, the rate of proline uptake increased significantly and to a greater extent than glutamine, which also increased in both primary bone marrow stromal cell and calvarial cultures (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by radiolabeled amino acid uptake assays shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The uptake of alanine was unchanged during differentiation.
source: By comparison, the uptake of alanine was unchanged during differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by amino acid uptake assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Proline carbon was not observed in glutamate or any other amino acid or other downstream metabolites (e.g., α−ketoglutarate, malate, or citrate) even after 72 hr.
source: The tracing experiments indicated that little proline metabolism occurs in osteoblasts as proline carbon was not observed in glutamate or any other amino acid or other downstream metabolites (e.g., α−ketoglutarate, malate, or citrate) even after 72 hr (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing experiments shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Carbon from both glutamine and glucose was observed in many metabolites, including α−ketoglutarate, malate, citrate, and various amino acids.
source: By comparison, carbon from both glutamine and glucose was observed in many metabolites, including α−ketoglutarate, malate, citrate, and various amino acids (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing experiments shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Proline is not metabolized to glutamate or other downstream metabolites.
source: These data suggest that proline is not metabolized to glutamate or other downstream metabolites.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from isotope tracing data showing lack of proline-derived label in downstream metabolites.

claim: Proline is primarily used for protein synthesis.
source: Rather, proline is primarily used for protein synthesis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from isotope tracing and protein incorporation data.

claim: Proline incorporation into both total protein and collagen significantly increases during differentiation.
source: Consistent with this conclusion, proline incorporation into both total protein and collagen significantly increases during differentiation (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by radiolabeled proline incorporation assays shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Almost 50% of the proline in total protein was derived from 13CU-proline.
source: Moreover, almost 50% of the proline in total protein was derived from 13CU-proline (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing into protein shown in Figure 2E.

claim: No proline-derived amino acids were observed in total protein despite the presence of glutamine-derived amino acids including proline.
source: Importantly, we observed no proline-derived amino acids in total protein despite the presence of glutamine-derived amino acids including proline (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing analysis of protein-incorporated amino acids shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Proline demand and protein synthesis rise concomitantly during osteoblast differentiation.
source: Thus, proline demand and protein synthesis rise concomitantly during osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations including uptake and incorporation assays.

claim: Proline withdrawal specifically reduced charging of the proline tRNA (AGG) but did not affect the activation of either the mTOR pathway or the integrated stress response (ISR).
source: Proline withdrawal specifically reduced charging of the proline tRNA (AGG) but did not affect the activation of either the mTOR pathway (as determined by S6 ribosomal protein phosphorylation at S235/236) or the integrated stress response (ISR) (as determined by EIF2α phosphorylation at Ser51) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by tRNA charging assays and Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Proline withdrawal did not affect the expression of select non-proline-enriched proteins.
source: Proline withdrawal did not affect the expression of select non-proline-enriched proteins (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Proline withdrawal significantly reduced the expression of osteoblast proteins that had higher-than-average proline content, including COL1A1 (19.1% proline), RUNX2 (10.5% proline), OSX (13.3% proline), and ATF4 (10.6% proline).
source: Conversely, proline withdrawal significantly reduced the expression of osteoblast proteins that had higher-than-average proline content, including COL1A1 (19.1% proline), RUNX2 (10.5% proline), OSX (13.3% proline), and ATF4 (10.6% proline) (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Proline withdrawal did not affect the mRNA expression of proline-enriched proteins.
source: Importantly, proline withdrawal did not affect the mRNA expression of these proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Proline withdrawal significantly reduced the expression of proline-enriched proteins (e.g., EIF4EBP1, PAX1, ATF2, SMAD1, and EIF2A) without affecting low proline proteins (ERK1, PHGDH, EEF2, AKT, ACTB, mTOR, TUBA, and S6RP).
source: We next took a candidate approach and evaluated other proline-enriched (e.g., EIF4EBP1 [13.7% proline], PAX1 [11.1% proline], ATF2 [10.7% proline], SMAD1 [9.9% proline], and EIF2A [7.6% proline]) and non-enriched proteins (ERK1 [6.6% proline], PHGDH [5.3% proline], EEF2 [5.2% proline], AKT [4.6% proline], ACTB [5.1% proline], mTOR [4.4% proline], TUBA [4.4% proline], and S6RP [4.2% proline]) that are not known to be required for osteoblast differentiation but are expressed in calvarial cells according to our transcriptomic analyses. Proline withdrawal significantly reduced the expression of the proline-enriched proteins without affecting the low proline proteins (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis of multiple proteins shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The reduction in protein expression significantly correlated with the proline content in the proteins.
source: The reduction in protein expression significantly correlated with the proline content in the proteins (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The decreased protein expression is due primarily to reduced synthesis of proline-enriched proteins.
source: The decreased protein expression is due primarily to reduced synthesis of proline-enriched proteins as cycloheximide (CHX) washout experiments found that proline withdrawal resulted in a significant delay in the recovery of proline-enriched protein expression (Figure 3C–G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by cycloheximide washout experiments shown in Figure 3C–G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–F.

claim: Proline is essential for the synthesis of proline-enriched osteoblast proteins.
source: Thus, proline is essential for the synthesis of proline-enriched osteoblast proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations showing reduced synthesis of proline-enriched proteins upon proline withdrawal.

claim: MeAIB reduced proline uptake by 80% in both osteoblasts and bone shafts with minimal effects on the uptake of other amino acids (e.g., Gln, Ala, Gly, or Ser).
source: Consistent with these reports, MeAIB reduced proline uptake by 80% in both osteoblasts and bone shafts with minimal effects on the uptake of other amino acids (e.g., Gln, Ala, Gly, or Ser) (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by amino acid uptake assays with MeAIB inhibitor shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Slc38a2 is the highest expressed putative proline transporter in calvarial cells.
source: Evaluation of our transcriptomic data identified Slc38a2 as the highest expressed putative proline transporter in calvarial cells (Table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis shown in Table 3.

claim: Slc38a2 encodes the sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter-2 (SNAT2), which transports neutral alpha amino acids (e.g., proline) in a Na+-dependent manner that is sensitive to MeAIB.
source: Slc38a2 encodes the sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter-2 (SNAT2, denoted here as SLC38A2), which transports neutral alpha amino acids (e.g., proline) in a Na+-dependent manner that is sensitive to MeAIB (Grewal et al., 2009; Hoffmann et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Grewal et al., 2009; Hoffmann et al., 2018).

claim: Slc38a2 targeting significantly reduced SLC38A2 protein and reduced radiolabeled proline uptake by ~50% in differentiated calvarial cells.
source: Slc38a2 targeting significantly reduced SLC38A2 protein and reduced radiolabeled proline uptake by ~50% in differentiated calvarial cells (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by CRISPR/Cas9 targeting experiments and uptake assays shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Proline and glutamine were both reduced by Slc38a2 ablation, whereas no other amino acid was significantly affected by the loss of SLC38A2.
source: Next, we evaluated the effects of Slc38a2 ablation on intracellular amino acid concentration using mass spectrometry. Proline and glutamine were both reduced, whereas no other amino acid was significantly affected by the loss of SLC38A2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The reduction in glutamine concentration is attributed to a compensatory increase in de novo proline synthesis from glutamine in the SLC38A2-deficient cells.
source: The reduction in glutamine concentration is attributed to a compensatory increase in de novo proline synthesis from glutamine in the SLC38A2-deficient cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from isotope tracing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Slc38a2 ablation specifically reduced proline-tRNA charging similar to proline withdrawal without negatively affecting charging of other tRNAs or activating the ISR.
source: Consistent with decreased proline uptake, Slc38a2 ablation specifically reduced proline-tRNA charging similar to proline withdrawal without negatively affecting charging of other tRNAs or activating the ISR (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by tRNA charging assays and Western blot analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Slc38a2 ablation specifically reduced the expression of the proline-enriched proteins without affecting the expression of non-proline-enriched proteins or the mRNA expression of these proteins.
source: Moreover, Slc38a2 ablation specifically reduced the expression of the proline-enriched proteins without affecting the expression of non-proline-enriched proteins or the mRNA expression of these proteins (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot and qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: The effect of Slc38a2 ablation on protein expression significantly correlated with the proline content in the proteins.
source: The effect of Slc38a2 ablation on protein expression significantly correlated with the proline content in the proteins (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Slc38a2-deficient cells were characterized by significantly reduced rates of collagen synthesis and protein synthesis in general.
source: Importantly, Slc38a2-deficient cells were characterized by significantly reduced rates of collagen synthesis and protein synthesis in general (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by protein and collagen synthesis assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H and I.

claim: Slc38a2 deletion did not affect either mTOR activation or induce ISR.
source: This is likely a direct result of decreased proline uptake as Slc38a2 deletion did not affect either mTOR activation or induce ISR (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: SLC38A2 provides proline for the efficient synthesis of proline-enriched proteins.
source: Thus, SLC38A2 provides proline for the efficient synthesis of proline-enriched proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations showing reduced proline uptake and protein synthesis upon Slc38a2 ablation.

claim: Slc38a2 deletion did not affect cell viability, proliferation, or the mRNA expression or induction of early osteoblast regulatory genes (e.g., Akp2 and Runx2).
source: Slc38a2 deletion did not affect cell viability, proliferation, or the mRNA expression or induction of early osteoblast regulatory genes (e.g., Akp2 and Runx2) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell viability, proliferation, and gene expression assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Slc38a2-deficient cells were characterized by reduced induction of Sp7 and terminal osteoblast marker genes (e.g., Ibsp and Bglap) as well as reduced matrix mineralization.
source: However, Slc38a2-deficient cells were characterized by reduced induction of Sp7 and terminal osteoblast marker genes (e.g., Ibsp and Bglap) as well as reduced matrix mineralization (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression and functional assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: SLC38A2 provides proline required for terminal osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization in vitro.
source: This indicates that SLC38A2 provides proline required for terminal osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization in vitro.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from in vitro differentiation and mineralization assays.

claim: Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ embryos were characterized by a conspicuous reduction in red mineralized bone matrix staining in both endochondral and intramembranous bones at embryonic day (E)15.5.
source: Using Alcian blue and Alizarin red staining (which stains cartilage and bone matrix blue or red, respectively), we found that Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ embryos were characterized by a conspicuous reduction in red mineralized bone matrix staining in both endochondral and intramembranous bones at embryonic day (E)15.5 (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparations shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: The defect in bone mineralization was most obvious in the developing skull of Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ animals.
source: This defect in bone mineralization was most obvious in the developing skull (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparations shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ animals had no apparent defects in cartilage formation at E15.5.
source: By comparison, Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ animals had no apparent defects in cartilage formation at E15.5, indicating that loss of Slc38a2 impacts osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparations and histological analysis.

claim: Loss of Slc38a2 impacts osteoblast differentiation.
source: By comparison, Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ animals had no apparent defects in cartilage formation at E15.5, indicating that loss of Slc38a2 impacts osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that cartilage is normal but bone is affected in Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ animals.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl bones were characterized by reduced SLC38A2 expression and reduced proline uptake.
source: Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl bones were characterized by reduced SLC38A2 expression and reduced proline uptake (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot and uptake assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice had significantly less Alizarin red-stained bone matrix at E15.5.
source: Like the Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ mice, Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice had significantly less Alizarin red-stained bone matrix at E15.5 (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparations shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: By postnatal day 1 (P1), overall bone matrix in long bones was comparable in both Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ and Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl genetic models.
source: By postnatal day 1 (P1), overall bone matrix in long bones was comparable in both genetic models; however, the skulls from both Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ and Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice continued to be poorly mineralized with patent fontanelles compared to their respective littermate controls (Figure 5E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparations shown in Figure 5E–H and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The skulls from both Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ and Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice continued to be poorly mineralized with patent fontanelles at P1 compared to their respective littermate controls.
source: By postnatal day 1 (P1), overall bone matrix in long bones was comparable in both genetic models; however, the skulls from both Slc38a2LacZ/LacZ and Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice continued to be poorly mineralized with patent fontanelles compared to their respective littermate controls (Figure 5E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparations shown in Figure 5E–H and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl calvariae had normal alkaline phosphatase staining despite less mineralized area shown by von Kossa staining.
source: Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl calvariae had normal alkaline phosphatase staining despite less mineralized area shown by von Kossa staining (Figure 5I–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological staining shown in Figure 5I–L.

claim: The defects in bone development are attributed to delayed osteoblast differentiation as Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice had significantly reduced expression of Spp1, Ibsp, and Bglap.
source: The defects in bone development are attributed to delayed osteoblast differentiation as Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice had significantly reduced expression of Spp1, Ibsp, and Bglap (Figure 5M–R).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 5M–R.

claim: There was no difference in the total number of Sp7:GFP expressing cells per mineralized area in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl animals.
source: This was not due to a reduction in overall osteoblast numbers as there was no difference in the total number of Sp7:GFP expressing cells per mineralized area (Figure 5S–T).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5S–T.

claim: Significantly fewer Sp7:GFP-expressing cells were found to have OSX or RUNX2 protein expression in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl animals.
source: Despite this, significantly fewer Sp7:GFP-expressing cells were found to have OSX (encoded by Sp7) or RUNX2 protein expression in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl animals (Figure 5S-T, Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5S-T and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Sp7GFP-expressing cells in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice had significantly reduced COL1A1 protein expression despite normal Col1a1 mRNA expression when compared to Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/+ controls.
source: Similarly, Sp7GFP-expressing cells in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice had significantly reduced COL1A1 protein expression despite normal Col1a1 mRNA expression when compared to Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/+ controls (Figure 5U–X, Figure 5—figure supplements 2B and 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence and in situ hybridization shown in Figure 5U–X and Figure 5—figure supplements 2B and 3C.

claim: The expression of proline-poor actin (as determined by phalloidin staining) and GFP (4.2% proline) were unaffected in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl calvariae.
source: For comparison, the expression of proline-poor actin (as determined by phalloidin staining) and GFP (4.2% proline) were unaffected in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl calvariae (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Slc38a2 provides proline essential for osteoblast differentiation and bone formation during bone development.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that Slc38a2 provides proline essential for osteoblast differentiation and bone formation during bone development.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple in vivo experiments showing bone defects in Slc38a2 mutant mice.

claim: Osteoblasts require proline to fulfill unique biosynthetic demands that arise due to increased production of proline-enriched osteoblast-associated proteins.
source: Here, we have defined a specific requirement for proline that arises during osteoblast differentiation and bone formation. Namely, that osteoblasts require proline to fulfill unique biosynthetic demands that arise due to increased production of proline-enriched osteoblast-associated proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations throughout the study.

claim: Osteoblasts significantly increase proline consumption during differentiation to fulfill increased proline demand.
source: To fulfill this demand, osteoblasts significantly increase proline consumption during differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by proline uptake assays showing increased uptake during differentiation.

claim: Genetically limiting proline uptake by ablating the proline transporter SLC38A2 results in delayed bone development.
source: Genetically limiting proline uptake by ablating the proline transporter SLC38A2 results in delayed bone development.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo experiments with Slc38a2 mutant mice.

claim: Osteoblasts utilize proline primarily for the synthesis of proline-enriched osteoblast proteins to facilitate both osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production.
source: Mechanistically, osteoblasts utilize proline primarily for the synthesis of proline-enriched osteoblast proteins to facilitate both osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from isotope tracing and protein synthesis experiments.

claim: There is a broad requirement for proline to regulate osteoblast differentiation and bone development in addition to supporting collagen synthesis.
source: Collectively, these data highlight a broad requirement for proline to regulate osteoblast differentiation and bone development in addition to supporting collagen synthesis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the comprehensive set of experiments showing proline's role beyond collagen synthesis.

claim: Osteoblast differentiation is characterized by a distinct protein profile in addition to increasing bone matrix production.
source: Osteoblast differentiation is characterized by a distinct protein profile in addition to increasing bone matrix production (Alves et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Alves et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2007).

claim: Osteoblast-associated proteins are enriched for the amino acid proline compared to all other proteins.
source: These osteoblast-associated proteins are enriched for the amino acid proline compared to all other proteins (Figure 1, Tables 1–2).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 1 and Tables 1–2.

claim: Increased consumption of numerous amino acids in differentiating osteoblasts has been described, including glutamine, asparagine, and proline.
source: We and others have recently described increased consumption of numerous amino acids in differentiating osteoblasts including glutamine (Sharma et al., 2021; Stegen et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2019), asparagine (Sharma et al., 2021), and proline (this study).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent literature and the current study.

claim: Glutamine and asparagine contribute to both de novo amino acid biosynthesis and protein synthesis directly.
source: Glutamine and asparagine contribute to both de novo amino acid biosynthesis and protein synthesis directly (Sharma et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature (Sharma et al., 2021).

claim: Proline can be oxidized in the inner mitochondrial membrane to form pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) by proline dehydrogenase (PRODH).
source: In addition to being directly incorporated into protein, proline can be oxidized in the inner mitochondrial membrane to form pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) by proline dehydrogenase (PRODH).
evidence: The claim is based on established biochemical knowledge about proline metabolism.

claim: PRODH is a flavin dinucleotide (FAD)-dependent enzyme that donates electrons to complex II of the electron transport chain coupling proline oxidation to ATP synthesis.
source: PRODH is a flavin dinucleotide (FAD)-dependent enzyme that donates electrons to complex II of the electron transport chain coupling proline oxidation to ATP synthesis (Elia et al., 2017; Liu and Phang, 2012b; Olivares et al., 2017; Phang et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Elia et al., 2017; Liu and Phang, 2012b; Olivares et al., 2017; Phang et al., 2012).

claim: P5C can be converted back into proline by the NADPH-dependent enzyme pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase (PYCR) in the proline cycle or can be converted into glutamate or other intermediate metabolites.
source: P5C can be converted back into proline by the NADPH-dependent enzyme pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase (PYCR) in the proline cycle or can be converted into glutamate or other intermediate metabolites.
evidence: The claim is based on established biochemical knowledge about proline metabolism.

claim: Tracing experiments did not find proline carbon enriched in either amino acids or trichloroacetic acid (TCA) intermediates.
source: Our tracing experiments did not find proline carbon enriched in either amino acids or trichloroacetic acid (TCA) intermediates.
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing experiments.

claim: Proline is not widely metabolized past P5C in osteoblasts.
source: For this reason, we conclude that proline is not widely metabolized past P5C in osteoblasts, but we are unable to make any conclusions about proline oxidation or the contribution of proline to bioenergetics in osteoblasts.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from isotope tracing data, with acknowledgment of technical limitations.

claim: The primary use for proline is direct incorporation into nascent protein.
source: Rather, our data indicates the primary use for proline is direct incorporation into nascent protein.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from isotope tracing and protein incorporation data.

claim: Reducing proline availability specifically reduced the synthesis of proteins with higher-than-average proline content without affecting mTOR activation or inducing ISR.
source: Consistent with this, reducing proline availability specifically reduced the synthesis of proteins with higher-than-average proline content without affecting mTOR activation or inducing ISR (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by protein synthesis and signaling pathway analysis shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Proline depletion likely results in stalling of proline codons of proline-enriched genes at both the A and P sites of the ribosome similar to clear cell renal cell carcinoma that are vulnerable to proline depletion.
source: Proline depletion likely results in stalling of proline codons of proline-enriched genes at both the A and P sites of the ribosome similar to clear cell renal cell carcinoma that are vulnerable to proline depletion (Loayza-Puch et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the current data and comparison to previous literature (Loayza-Puch et al., 2016).

claim: Protein expression was negatively correlated with the proline content in proteins when proline availability or uptake was limited.
source: Consistent with this, protein expression was negatively correlated with the proline content in proteins when proline availability or uptake was limited (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Limiting the availability of glutamine-induced robust activation of the ISR inhibits global protein synthesis.
source: By comparison, limiting the availability of glutamine-induced robust activation of the ISR inhibits global protein synthesis (Sharma et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature (Sharma et al., 2021).

claim: Glutamine metabolism is necessary to maintain amino acid concentrations (including proline) and provide other metabolites during osteoblast differentiation.
source: This likely reflects the necessity of glutamine metabolism to maintain amino acid concentrations (including proline) and provide other metabolites during osteoblast differentiation (Sharma et al., 2021; Stegen et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Sharma et al., 2021; Stegen et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2019).

claim: Activation of the ISR was not observed in proline-free conditions despite reduced charging of proline tRNA.
source: Consistent with the more direct use of proline in protein but not amino acid biosynthesis, we did not observe activation of the ISR in proline-free conditions despite reduced charging of proline tRNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by tRNA charging and ISR marker analysis.

claim: De novo biosynthesis of proline may be sufficient to meet the basal needs of naïve calvarial cells under proline withdrawal for 48 hr.
source: Under these conditions, de novo biosynthesis of proline may be sufficient to meet the basal needs of naïve calvarial cells.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on the observation that ISR is not activated despite proline withdrawal.

claim: Proline removal results in reduced synthetic efficiency of proline-rich proteins.
source: Regardless, proline removal results in reduced synthetic efficiency of proline-rich proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from protein synthesis experiments.

claim: The effect of proline removal on protein synthesis is likely exacerbated during osteoblast differentiation as proline-rich proteins are increased.
source: This effect is likely exacerbated during osteoblast differentiation as these proline-rich proteins are increased.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on the observation that proline-rich proteins increase during differentiation.

claim: Previous studies described proline uptake occurring primarily via System A but did not identify individual transporters mediating proline uptake.
source: Previous studies characterized proline uptake in both bones and osteoblasts directly. These studies described proline uptake occurring primarily via System A but did not identify individual transporters mediating proline uptake (Adamson and Ingbar, 1967; Finerman and Rosenberg, 1966; Hahn et al., 1969; Yee, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Adamson and Ingbar, 1967; Finerman and Rosenberg, 1966; Hahn et al., 1969; Yee, 1988).

claim: SLC38A2 is responsible for approximately 55% of proline uptake in both calvarial osteoblasts and isolated bones.
source: Here, we identified the sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter SLC38A2 as responsible for approximately 55% of proline uptake in both calvarial osteoblasts and isolated bones (Figure 4B, Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by uptake assays shown in Figure 4B and Figure 5—figure supplement 3B.

claim: System A mediates 60% of proline uptake in osteoblasts.
source: This is consistent with previous reports that System A mediates 60% of proline uptake in osteoblasts (Yee, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature (Yee, 1988).

claim: SLC38A2 ablation affected only proline uptake.
source: Interestingly, SLC38A2 ablation affected only proline uptake (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by amino acid uptake assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B.

claim: SLC38A2 is reported to transport alanine, serine, glycine, and glutamine in different cellular contexts.
source: For example, SLC38A2 is reported to transport alanine, serine, glycine, and glutamine in different cellular contexts (Bröer et al., 2016; Morotti et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Bröer et al., 2016; Morotti et al., 2019).

claim: Glutamine is not a primary substrate for SLC38A2 in bone cells.
source: Our data indicates that glutamine is not a primary substrate for SLC38A2 in bone cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from uptake assays showing no effect of SLC38A2 ablation on glutamine uptake.

claim: Glutamine uptake is mediated primarily by System ASC with no involvement of System A in osteoblasts.
source: This is consistent with our recent data demonstrating that glutamine uptake is mediated primarily by System ASC with no involvement of System A in osteoblasts (Sharma et al., 2021; Shen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent literature (Sharma et al., 2021; Shen et al., 2021).

claim: Reducing proline uptake inhibited bone development in mice.
source: Reducing proline uptake inhibited bone development in mice (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The bone development phenotype was attributed primarily to decreased osteoblast differentiation and reduced bone matrix production.
source: This phenotype was attributed primarily to decreased osteoblast differentiation and reduced bone matrix production.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from histological and molecular analyses of mutant mice.

claim: Osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production are associated with a unique biosynthetic demand for proline.
source: Osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production are associated with a unique biosynthetic demand for proline.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from bioinformatic and experimental data throughout the study.

claim: Osteoblast-associated proteins are more enriched for proline than any other amino acid when compared to other cell types.
source: Using a bioinformatic approach, we discovered that osteoblast-associated proteins are more enriched for proline than any other amino acid when compared to other cell types (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Many proline-rich proteins are essential regulators of osteoblast differentiation (e.g., RUNX2, OSX, and ATF4), bone matrix production (e.g., COL1A1), or regulate the endocrine functions of bone (e.g., OCN).
source: Many of these proline-rich proteins are essential regulators of osteoblast differentiation (e.g., RUNX2, OSX, and ATF4), bone matrix production (e.g., COL1A1), or regulate the endocrine functions of bone (e.g., OCN) (Ducy et al., 1996; Ducy et al., 1997; Elefteriou et al., 2006; Kern et al., 2001; Nakashima et al., 2002; Otto et al., 1997; Yang et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Ducy et al., 1996; Ducy et al., 1997; Elefteriou et al., 2006; Kern et al., 2001; Nakashima et al., 2002; Otto et al., 1997; Yang et al., 2004).

claim: Limiting proline availability by genetically ablating SLC38A2 specifically affected the production of proline-rich proteins (e.g., RUNX2, OSX, and COL1A1) in a manner that was proportional to the relative proline content.
source: Limiting proline availability by genetically ablating SLC38A2 specifically affected the production of proline-rich proteins (e.g., RUNX2, OSX, and COL1A1) in a manner that was proportional to the relative proline content.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis and correlation analysis.

claim: Relatively minor reductions in protein expression or function are known to negatively impact osteoblast differentiation and bone development and underlie human bone diseases.
source: It is important to note that relatively minor reductions in protein expression or function are known to negatively impact osteoblast differentiation and bone development and underlie human bone diseases (Baek et al., 2013; Bardai et al., 2016; Ben Amor et al., 2013; Choi et al., 2001; Lapunzina et al., 2010; Lee et al., 1997; Lou et al., 2009; Mundlos et al., 1997; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Baek et al., 2013; Bardai et al., 2016; Ben Amor et al., 2013; Choi et al., 2001; Lapunzina et al., 2010; Lee et al., 1997; Lou et al., 2009; Mundlos et al., 1997; Zhang et al., 2009).

claim: Ablating SLC38A2-dependent proline uptake has broad effects on osteoblast differentiation due to minor reductions in many proline-rich osteoblast regulatory proteins.
source: Thus, ablating SLC38A2-dependent proline uptake has broad effects on osteoblast differentiation due to minor reductions in many proline-rich osteoblast regulatory proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that multiple proline-rich proteins are reduced in SLC38A2-deficient cells.

claim: When proline is available, osteoblast progenitors efficiently synthesize the proline-rich proteins necessary for differentiation (RUNX2 and OSX) and bone matrix deposition (COL1A1).
source: When proline is available, osteoblast progenitors efficiently synthesize the proline-rich proteins necessary for differentiation (RUNX2 and OSX) and bone matrix deposition (COL1A1).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from protein synthesis experiments.

claim: The high proline content of osteoblast proteins presents a novel cellular checkpoint to ascertain if appropriate resources, in this case proline, are available for osteoblast differentiation to proceed.
source: The high proline content of these proteins presents a novel cellular checkpoint to ascertain if appropriate resources, in this case proline, are available for osteoblast differentiation to proceed.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on the observation that proline-rich protein synthesis is sensitive to proline availability.

claim: When proline is limited, proline-rich proteins are not efficiently synthesized, which limits osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production until sufficient proline is available.
source: When proline is limited, these proteins are not efficiently synthesized, which limits osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production until sufficient proline is available.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from protein synthesis and differentiation experiments.

claim: This mechanism is critical to ensure that cells can meet the synthetic challenges associated with osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production.
source: This is critical to ensure that cells can meet the synthetic challenges associated with osteoblast differentiation and bone matrix production.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference about the biological significance of the findings.

claim: Delayed COLX remodeling was observed in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice.
source: In addition to the aforementioned osteoblast defects, we also observed delayed COLX remodeling in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis.

claim: Loss of SLC38A2 in hypertrophic chondrocytes contributes to delayed endochondral ossification in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice.
source: This suggests that loss of SLC38A2 in hypertrophic chondrocytes contributes to delayed endochondral ossification in Sp7Cre;Slc38a2fl/fl mice.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation of delayed COLX remodeling.

claim: SLC38A2 may provide chondrocytes with proline (or other amino acids) to facilitate the production of proline-rich collagens (e.g., COL2 and COLX) or other proteins during chondrogenesis and endochondral ossification.
source: It is intriguing to speculate that SLC38A2 provides chondrocytes with proline (or other amino acids) to facilitate the production of proline-rich collagens (e.g., COL2 and COLX) or other proteins during chondrogenesis and endochondral ossification.
evidence: The claim is explicitly speculative about the role of SLC38A2 in chondrocytes.

claim: SLC38A2 acts cell-autonomously in osteoblasts to provide proline.
source: In summary, we have defined the necessity and the molecular substrates of Slc38a2 in osteoblasts. Our data indicate that SLC38A2 acts cell-autonomously in osteoblasts to provide proline and that SLC38A2 is the major proline transporter in osteoblasts.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from genetic ablation experiments showing cell-autonomous effects.

claim: SLC38A2 is the major proline transporter in osteoblasts.
source: In summary, we have defined the necessity and the molecular substrates of Slc38a2 in osteoblasts. Our data indicate that SLC38A2 acts cell-autonomously in osteoblasts to provide proline and that SLC38A2 is the major proline transporter in osteoblasts.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from uptake assays showing SLC38A2 mediates ~55% of proline uptake.

claim: Proline is essential for the production of proline-rich transcription factors (e.g., RUNX2 and OSX) and matrix proteins (COL1A1) necessary for osteoblast differentiation and bone formation.
source: Proline is essential for the production of proline-rich transcription factors (e.g., RUNX2 and OSX) and matrix proteins (COL1A1) necessary for osteoblast differentiation and bone formation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations showing reduced expression of these proteins upon proline limitation.

claim: The data expand our understanding of the regulation of proline uptake and usage in osteoblasts.
source: These data expand our understanding of the regulation of proline uptake and usage in osteoblasts and underscore the necessity of proline for osteoblast differentiation and bone development.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: The data underscore the necessity of proline for osteoblast differentiation and bone development.
source: These data expand our understanding of the regulation of proline uptake and usage in osteoblasts and underscore the necessity of proline for osteoblast differentiation and bone development.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the comprehensive experimental evidence presented.
